Run a quick endpoint scan on Tommy’s workstation for any recent credential‑theft tools or browser extensions that might have been installed via similar bulk phishing attempts.
Add zoomcall-invites.com to the organization’s threat‑intel watchlist and configure a temporary block or sandbox redirect in the web proxy until further reputation data is gathered.
Update Mimecast policies to flag future messages from this sender domain with higher severity (e.g., ‘high’ instead of ‘medium’) and require manual release only after analyst review.
Log the source IP (40.107.92.115) in your SIEM and create a correlation rule that alerts on any subsequent connections from this address to internal assets, even if the provider is currently unknown.
Consider reaching out to Zoom’s security team or abuse contact to report the suspicious invite domain; they may have visibility into compromised accounts being abused for phishing.

Document the incident in the central ticketing system with all enrichment details and note that no malicious payload was observed, but maintain the case open for 30 days to monitor for repeat activity.
